newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline, diesel prices rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline, diesel prices rise.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel prices rose on Thursday, fueled by higher NYMEX futures prices, traders said.
Gasoline and diesel differentials were unchanged on the day in thin trade, leaving prices to track underlying NYMEX unleaded and heating oil contracts.
Shipping delays on the Houston-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline system that pushed liftings back by five days earlier this week were not a factor in the market.
"It's really been quiet today," a Group Three trader said. "I think the market is really well balanced."
Low sulphur diesel remained bid 2.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX May heating oil in Chicago and 6.0 cents over the print in Group Three, traders said.
High sulphur also was unchanged at 1.50/1.75 cents over the print in Chicago and 5.75/6.0 cents over the print in Group Three, traders said.
Unleaded gasoline differentials were unchanged at 0.25 cent a gallon under to even with NYMEX May unleaded in Chicago and 0.50/0.25 cent under the print in Group Three, traders said.
